# Reference vectors for kernels-metal/kernels/rope/neox.metal.
# produced by crates/driver-metal/tests/fixtures/cuda_reference.cu (regenerate with run.sh beside it)
# gpu: NVIDIA L40S, sm_89
# nvcc: 13.0.88
# built: Aug 25 2026
#
# Arrays are named for the CUDA kernel's own parameters, IN LOWER CASE: a name in this
# format is [a-z0-9_], so `I`, `K`, `E`, `R` and `C` are written `i`, `k`, `e`, `r` and `c`.
# Every f32 token is the little-endian bit pattern of the value; a bf16 operand is recorded
# as the f32 its sixteen bits widen to, so the Metal side loads the same bits after narrowing.
# A scalar is an array of length 1.
#
# N = 3 tokens, n_head = 5, head_dim = 24, theta = 10000, positions = {1, 6, 23}.
# Every rotation is in place: `q_in` is the buffer as launched, `q_out` as it came back,
# both [N, n_head, head_dim]. num_kv_heads is 0 throughout -- the Metal kernels turn one tensor.
#
# neox_mb_full             <- pie::rope::rotate<false, false>(q, k=q, positions, num_q_heads=5, num_kv_heads=0, head_dim=24, theta=10000, interleaved=false, cache_pairs, heads_per_block, ...)
# neox_mb_partial          <- the same kernel at head_dim=16 over the leading 16 channels of each head, then scattered back (see below)
# neox_prop_mb             <- pie::rope::rotate_partial<bf16>(q, k=q, positions, position_delta=0, num_q_heads=5, num_kv_heads=0, head_dim=24, rotary_dim=16, theta=10000)
# neox_last_mb             <- pie::rope::rotate_partial_last(q, k=q, positions, num_q_heads=5, num_kv_heads=0, head_dim=24, rotary_dim=16, theta=10000, inverse=false, interleaved=false, yarn_factor=1, 0, 0)
# neox_last_mb_interleaved <- the same with interleaved=true
# neox_yarn_mb             <- pie::rope::rotate_yarn_original(q, k=q, positions, num_q_heads=5, num_kv_heads=0, head_dim=24, theta=10000, factor, low_dim, high_dim, mscale, interleaved=false, heads_per_block, cache_pairs)
# neox_yarn_mb_interleaved <- the same with interleaved=true
#
# THE PARTIAL CASE IS A REPACK, and it is the only host arithmetic in this file that is not
# a launch parameter. rope_neox_mb at rotary < head_dim pairs (i, i + rotary/2) and divides
# the exponent by rotary; no CUDA kernel does that -- `rotate` and `rotate_partial` both pair
# (i, i + head_dim/2) over head_dim. The rotation depends only on (position, dim_pair) and the
# two loaded values, so `rotate` at head_dim=16 over a [N, n_head, 16] buffer holding the leading
# 16 channels of each head IS that rotation, channel for channel. q_in and q_out are recorded
# at the FULL [N, n_head, 24] layout with the tail copied through untouched, which is what the
# Metal kernel leaves behind.
#
# `base` is log2(theta): neox.metal binds the log where CUDA binds theta. `scale` is neox.metal's
# position multiplier, which rotate/rotate_partial do not have -- 1.0 here, the value at which the
# two are the same rotation. rope_neox_last_mb and rope_neox_yarn_mb take no scale on either side.
#
